title: Multiplication always makes bigger
statement: Multiplying always gives a result larger than the number you started with, so multiplying by a fraction cannot make a number smaller.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict whether a product will be larger or smaller than a factor, without calculating
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts the product of a number and a proper fraction is larger than the number

example.item: Without calculating, is 8 x 3/4 more or less than 8?

evidence_patterns.item_shape: choose the operation for a word problem with a fractional multiplier
evidence_patterns.signature: rejects multiplication because the answer must be smaller, and divides instead

example.item: A recipe uses 2/3 of a 6-cup bag of flour. How much flour is used? Which operation?

discriminators.vs_slip: A slip is one wrong prediction. The belief is stated as a rule and generalises to decimals (0.5 x 8 'must be more than 8'); it often coexists with math.frac.divide-makes-smaller.

vs.math.frac.divide-makes-smaller: Mirror belief; test each separately with prediction items for multiplication and division by a proper fraction.

resolved_by.label: CCSS 5.NF.B.4: multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction

sources.citation: Fischbein, E., Deri, M., Nello, M. S., & Marino, M. S. (1985). The role of implicit models in solving verbal problems in multiplication and division. Journal for Research in Mathematics Education, 16(1), 3-17.
sources.note: Implicit repeated-addition model of multiplication: the product must exceed the multiplicand.

sources.citation: Bell, A., Swan, M., & Taylor, G. (1981). Choice of operation in verbal problems with decimal numbers. Educational Studies in Mathematics, 12(4), 399-420.

sources.note: Direction-of-effect items show adults and children expecting multiplication to increase.
